description: The bar chart illustrates the annual number of hateful communication datasets published from 2012 to 2022, categorized by language scope—monolingual (“1” language, shown in blue) and multilingual (“2+” languages, shown in orange)—with the y-axis representing the number of datasets on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 100. From 2012 to 2016, only monolingual datasets were published, with counts remaining low (1–2 datasets per year). Starting in 2017, multilingual datasets began to appear, with 5 such datasets that year, while monolingual datasets rose to 20. The trend continues upward through 2021, with monolingual datasets peaking at approximately 120 in 2021 and multilingual datasets reaching around 20 in 2020 before declining slightly to 10 in 2021. In 2022, the monolingual bar appears in a lighter blue shade (possibly indicating a different category or annotation) and drops to about 30 datasets, while multilingual datasets fall to roughly 3. The chart visually confirms the caption’s claim that monolingual datasets dominate overall, but multilingual efforts emerged and grew significantly beginning around 2017.
